subject_relevance.value: Berkshire's stated intention to cap its Japanese trading-house holdings at 9.9% and hold them long term is part of the Japanese investment course Buffett publicly explained; the cap is a company commitment, not a personal purchase.
evidence_source_contents: 该公司将只收购这五家公司中任何一家至多9.9%的股份
伯克希尔哈撒韦公司表示，它打算长期持有在日本的投资
reasons: The source attributes the cap and holding intention to Berkshire, not to Buffett personally.
Buffett is identified as Berkshire's CEO in the same article, supporting indirect relevance.

subject_relevance.value: Berkshire's initial ~$1 billion Activision Blizzard purchase preceded Microsoft's announced acquisition and is the background to the later merger-arbitrage position Buffett described; the source does not disclose whether Buffett or his lieutenants made the purchase.
evidence_source_contents: 于2021年第四季度花了近10亿美元购买了近1470万股动视暴雪的股票
也不清楚购买动视暴雪股票的是巴菲特还是他的两名投资副手的手笔
reasons: The purchase is attributed to Berkshire, with personal attribution explicitly unresolved.
It is the documented origin of the position Buffett later discussed as arbitrage.

subject_relevance.value: Buffett personally stated at Activision's annual meeting that Berkshire held about 9.5% of Activision and had been increasing the stake as a merger-arbitrage play, describing it as an occasional arbitrage trade he does himself.
evidence_source_contents: 巴菲特说，伯克希尔目前持有动视约9.5％的股份。
“偶尔我会看到套利交易，就去做，”伯克希尔的董事长兼首席执行官说。
reasons: Direct quotation attributes the arbitrage framing and decision to Buffett personally.
The stake increase is described as ongoing since the deal announcement.

subject_relevance.value: Berkshire disclosed a reduced 1.9% Activision stake, and the source links Buffett to the earlier merger-arbitrage buildup and to his long history of arbitrage trades with Munger.
evidence_source_contents: 其持有动视1.9%的股份，共计14658121股。相比之下，3月底的持股比例为6.3%，2022年底的持股比例为6.7%。
此后，这位92岁的投资传奇人物在一场并购套利游戏中增持了该公司的股份
reasons: The reduction is disclosed as Berkshire's holding, while Buffett is linked to the arbitrage buildup.
The source preserves the distinction between company disclosure and Buffett's stated arbitrage activity.

subject_relevance.value: Buffett's February 2023 shareholder letter advocated operating earnings over GAAP measures and called GAAP earnings '100 percent misleading when viewed quarterly or even annually,' while Berkshire reported its 2022 results.
evidence_source_contents: In his annual  letter to shareholders published on Feb. 25, Buffett said he and Charlie Munger, his longtime business partner, prefer using operating earnings as a measure of financial performance.
“The GAAP earnings are 100 percent misleading when viewed quarterly or even annually,” Buffett wrote in the shareholder letter.
reasons: Direct quotation attributes the performance-measure advocacy to Buffett's letter.
Berkshire's reported results provide the company context for the letter.

Berkshire bought 2.1 million additional Occidental shares, raising its stake to 25.1%.

Occidental was Berkshire's sixth-largest holding at the time.
Praised Occidental CEO Vicki Hollub as an outstanding manager, noting her first job was at Cities Service, the company of the first stock Buffett bought in 1942.
Said he understood the math of the business but would not know what to do in the oil-field domain.
Told shareholders he was satisfied with the warrants Berkshire holds from the 2019 transaction that helped fund Occidental's acquisition of Anadarko.

Buffett said Berkshire had been increasing its Activision stake since the Microsoft deal was announced because the shares traded well below Microsoft's offer.
Buffett described the position as an occasional arbitrage trade he does himself and acknowledged Berkshire could lose a fairly large amount if the deal fails.
Buffett said Berkshire did not know in advance about Microsoft's plan to acquire Activision when it made the initial ~$1 billion purchase in Q4 2021.
